title: Rain on a wood: does it drip through, and does the drip read right?
question: One of these lets rain work down through the canopy a drop at a time; the other leaves it standing in the branches. Does the dripping one read as rain falling through a tree, or is the rate wrong — too fast to be a drip, or too slow to clear?
context_md: Same binary, same seed, same wood, rain pinned on throughout; one env switch is the only difference. Before this, 89-96% of every liquid cell in the world stood on living tissue, mean 55-70 rows above the floor and as high as 107 -- almost no rain reached the ground in a wood at all. At the shipped rate that falls to 61-69%, and the mean height to 28-51 rows. The rate is the one thing I cannot measure: 24 frames per drop was too slow to clear anything, 2 clears most but may read as water falling straight through rather than beading and dripping. 8 is the middle and is what these show. Watch for whether drops are visible as individual drops -- water and sky are both blue, so motion is the only thing that separates a droplet from a gap in the leaves.
